newsitem.title: USA: FOCUS-Union Pacific seeks to buy Pennzoil.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Union Pacific seeks to buy Pennzoil.

text.p: Union Pacific Resources Group Inc said early Monday it has renewed its attempt to acquire Pennzoil Co after its previous advances were rebuffed, offering a two-step cash and stock transaction valued at about $6.4 billion.

Union Pacific said in the first step, a Union Pacific subsidiary is offering a cash tender for 50.1 percent of Pennzoil's common shares starting today. Union Pacific will finance the cash tender offer with bank borrowings, it said.

The second step includes a tax-free exchange of shares for the remaining 49.9 percent. Each remaining Pennzoil share will be exchanged for a number of Union Pacific shares, determined, within a pricing collar of $25 to $30, by dividing $84 by the average of the closing prices of Union Pacific common stock for the 20 consecutive trading days ending five days before Pennzoil shareholders meet to vote on the merger.
If the Union Pacific exchange ratio price is less than $25 or greater than $30, the exchange ratio will be fixed at 3.36 shares, or 2.80 shares, respectively, it said.
The proposed transaction is valued at $84 per Pennzoil share, which ended down 1/8 at 59-5/8 a share on Friday.

"We believe that the merger of UPR and Pennzoil will create the premier independent exploration and production company in the U.S.," Union Pacific Chairman and Chief Executive Jack Messman said in a statement. "Driven by UPR's proven ability to drill and develop oil and gas properties quickly and efficiently, we are confident that UPR will create growth and value well beyond what Pennzoil can achieve on its own."
Union Pacific said the combined company would lead the industry in a number of performance measures, including drilling activity, production and cash flow.
The company said the deal would immediately increase cash flow per share. But it is expected to have a near-term dilutive effect on earnings per share.
Union Pacific and Pennzoil shareholders must approve the deal. The transaction is not conditioned upon financing.
Pennzoil did not immediately return a telephone call seeking comment.

Union Pacific Resources Chairman and Chief Executive Jack Messman has sent a letter to Pennzoil Chairman and Chief Executive James Pate, whom the company said in a statement has "repeatedly rebuffed UPR's efforts to have any serious discussion about a possible transaction."
Messman wrote in the letter "these two companies belong together."
His letter also mentioned that Pate in 1995 proposed a merger with UPR, when it was a subsidiary of Union Pacific Corp .
